findings.claim_broken: V6/V7: a layer-0 run from the scratch root with no stack gives 154 passed / 103 skipped
findings.evidence: My first run was `env -u INFRX_E2_NAMESPACE TMPDIR=<private> pytest -q -rfEs tests/integration` right after my stack was torn down, with none of my fake_vllm processes alive (checked with ps). It gave `1 failed, 153 passed, 103 skipped`: test_killing_the_engine_process_is_a_transport_failure_and_it_restarts failed with `RuntimeError: fake vLLM exited 3 during startup on port 55582: ... [Errno 98] ... address already in use`, raised at test_fake_vllm.py:327 on the FIRST start, not the restart. The test alone then passed 3/3, and a full rerun gave `154 passed, 103 skipped`. TEST_PORT = harness.PORTS['fake_vllm'] + 1, a fixed port per namespace that layer-0/1 runs bind without the preflight's port check. So another checkout running the e2-namespace fake-vLLM tests at the same moment collides. This is the same class as the lane's F-12 transient (Limit 6/8). I did not see the lane's e3bm70/71/64 transient: all 14 mutants were killed on the first attempt.
findings.minimal_fix: Record it as a known flake alongside Limit 6. A later round could give the fake vLLM tests an ephemeral port (bind port 0 and read it back), or run them under the namespace's port lock.

findings.claim_broken: J3 evidence: 'the half-up rule runs on the real store' (dr07c's fractional card)
findings.evidence: `python3 -c "from decimal import Decimal as D,ROUND_HALF_UP,ROUND_HALF_EVEN,ROUND_DOWN; x=D(1200)*D('400.0000125')/D(10**6)+D(340)*D(1200)/D(10**6); q=D('0.00000001'); print(x, x.quantize(q,ROUND_HALF_UP), x.quantize(q,ROUND_HALF_EVEN), x.quantize(q,ROUND_DOWN))"` prints `0.888000015 0.88800002 0.88800002 0.88800001`. db14 therefore kills truncation, which was the reviewer's mutant T and is J3's stated scope. But a half-even (banker's) rounding defect in infrx.debit_credit or in money.debit would give the same 0.88800002 and survive. Note that money.py's arithmetic context defaults to ROUND_HALF_EVEN, and only the explicit quantize uses ROUND_HALF_UP.
findings.minimal_fix: Optionally, add a second fractional usage or card whose 9th-decimal tie sits after an even digit (for example one yielding x.xxxxxxx25) so that half-up and half-even disagree. Otherwise word the claim as 'rounds rather than truncates'.
